title: Entrypoint substitutions interpret literal backslashes as regex replacement syntax
reasoning: Both replacement values are passed directly to re.Pattern.sub, which parses backslash escapes and group references. Valid command text containing a literal backslash-n is altered into a newline, while other backslash sequences can raise re.error. The substitution contract requires inserting the provided path and command literally.
reproduction: Pass an entry_command containing the literal characters '\\n', such as a printf command: the returned specification contains an actual newline instead. A replacement containing '\\1' raises an invalid group reference error.
recommendation: Use literal string replacement or callable regex replacements for both placeholders.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied placeholder test uses a simple filename and command without backslashes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Parameterize the existing placeholder scenario with paths and commands containing literal backslashes, escape sequences, and group-reference-like text; assert exact preservation.
minimumFixScope: Change replace_spec_placeholders and extend the existing prompt substitution test.
